name: application-flight-route-card
title: Flight Route Card
description: Flight search result card showing airline, flight number, stop count, origin/destination codes and times with a duration line between them, and the fare.
useWhen: Displaying a single flight option in a search results list, showing the route at a glance.
Users need origin/destination airport codes, departure/arrival times, duration, and stop count together.
The card needs to scan quickly across many similar results, so layout consistency matters more than exhaustive detail.
avoidWhen: You need full itinerary detail (seat class, baggage, layover airports) — this card is a compact summary; link out to a detail view for that.
The route has multiple legs that each need their own duration/stop breakdown — extend this pattern per-leg rather than cramming multiple segments into one card.
There's no fare to show — drop the price row rather than rendering an empty one.
responsiveBehavior: The card is a fixed max-w-sm block that fills its container's available width up to that cap at all breakpoints.
accessibility: Airport codes are paired with full city names in the footer row, so the route is understandable beyond three-letter codes alone.
The stop count badge uses both color and explicit text ('Nonstop'), never color alone to convey routing complexity.
Times include AM/PM and a '+1' suffix for next-day arrivals, avoiding ambiguity in a 12-hour format.

variants.title: Flight route card
variants.description: Nonstop SFO to NRT flight with airline, times, duration, route footer, and fare.
accessibility: The airline code badge is decorative shorthand; the full airline name is always present as adjacent text.

variants.title: Flight route card (Dark)
variants.description: Flight route card adapted for dark application surfaces.
accessibility: Stop-count badge and divider colors must meet WCAG AA contrast on dark surfaces.
